# sec-filing-ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: your partner's words, 2026-11-12. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md, specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). One uv workspace with four package scaffolds under `packages/` (sec-edgar-client, sec-edgar-download, sec-edgar-index-ingest, sec-edgar-ingest).

| # | Outcome | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | The quarterly and daily index files, ingested into one filing-index table | A | 1 | Small: about 130 quarterly files since 1993 plus one daily file per business day, minutes of downloading at 3 requests/second (basis: SEC full-index and daily-index directories); measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | The individual submissions that the index rows name, downloaded | A | 2 | Large: millions of files, weeks for the full history at 3 requests/second (basis: index row count × request rate; not yet measured) |
| O3 | 10-K and 8-K filings handled: picked out of the submissions, with their main documents extracted | A | 3 | Unknown until submissions are on disk (basis: none yet) |

Tracks: A — SEC filing ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

Order follows your ranking for O1–O3, which is also the dependency order: each outcome consumes the one before it. The later qualities come after, as hardening stages 4–7, ordered by dependency: traceability first, because point-in-time awareness, validation and deployment all rely on it.

- [ ] Stage 1: Index ingestion (core)
      Objective: Ingest real SEC quarterly and daily index files into one filing-index table at the smallest standard that gives a usable result.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (package scaffolds only)
      Produces: a filing-index table on disk covering the ingested range; specs/sec-filing-ingestion-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1 — the table holds rows from real quarterly and daily index files, and its row count matches the source files' data-row count. The findings file records the range ingested and the measured cost of the real run: requests issued, bytes downloaded, elapsed time.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Submission download
      Objective: Download the individual submissions that the filing-index rows name.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1's filing-index table
      Produces: submissions on disk, each linked to its index row; a list of the submissions that failed
      Exit: O2 — every submission named by an index row in the range that Stage 1 ingested is on disk or appears on the failure list, and the stage records its measured download rate and volume.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 3: 10-K and 8-K handling
      Objective: Pick 10-K and 8-K filings out of the downloaded submissions and extract their main documents.
      Outcomes: O3
      Consumes: Stage 2's submissions on disk and their index-row links
      Produces: extracted main documents for 10-K and 8-K filings, each linked to its submission
      Exit: O3 — the count of extracted 10-K and 8-K main documents matches the index's 10-K and 8-K rows among the downloaded submissions, and each shortfall is listed with its reason.
      Leaves out: manifests and traceability → Stage 4; point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 4: Manifests and traceability
      Objective: Make every index row, submission and extracted document traceable to the source bytes and the run that produced it, so outputs can be replayed from stored inputs.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: manifests and traceability)
      Consumes: Stages 1–3 outputs
      Produces: a manifest naming source, hash and producing run for each output; replay from stored inputs without SEC requests
      Exit: Each output of O1–O3 resolves through the manifest to its source bytes. A replay from stored inputs reproduces the same outputs with zero SEC requests.
      Leaves out: point-in-time awareness → Stage 5; full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Point-in-time awareness
      Objective: Make the filing index reflect later SEC changes to quarterly indexes while keeping what was known at each earlier point.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: point-in-time awareness)
      Consumes: Stage 4's manifest and replay
      Produces: versioned filing-index state, with additions, changes and withdrawals recorded against their source
      Exit: A re-read quarterly index that differs from its earlier copy yields a recorded change set, and the prior state stays readable.
      Leaves out: full validation suite → Stage 6; scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 6: Full validation suite
      Objective: Cover O1–O3 and the Stage 4–5 guarantees with fixture-based tests that make no SEC requests.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: full validation suite)
      Consumes: Stages 1–5 outputs
      Produces: committed fixtures and a CI test suite
      Exit: CI passes on committed fixtures covering index formats, submissions, 10-K and 8-K extraction, replay and change sets, with zero network requests.
      Leaves out: scheduling and deployment → Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 7: Scheduling and deployment
      Objective: Run daily index ingestion, submission download, 10-K and 8-K handling, and reconciliation on a schedule in a deployed environment.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O3 (hardening: scheduling and deployment)
      Consumes: Stage 6's passing suite; Stages 4–5's manifest and versioned state
      Produces: a deployed, scheduled pipeline with run reports
      Exit: Scheduled runs complete in the deployed environment, and their durable run reports show new daily sources ingested and gaps listed.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming
